# Axial: LLM context

## Product boundary

- `Flow<'env,'error,'value>` is a cold workflow description with explicit dependencies and typed expected failures.
- Axial does not depend on Reified; it binds standard F# `Result` and `Option` directly.
- Use `Flow<'value>`, `Flow<'error,'value>`, `EnvFlow<'env,'value>`, `ExnFlow<'value>`, or
  `ExnEnvFlow<'env,'value>` when the shorter channel combination is sufficient.

## Execution and dependencies

- Pass a record environment and read it with `Flow.envWith`.
- `Flow.env` is the whole environment; `Flow.envWith f` projects one value out of it. Readers who know ZIO, the Scala
  effect library with the same environment model, can map them to `ZIO.environment` and `ZIO.environmentWith`; a
  package's `service` accessor maps to `ZIO.service[A]`.
- `Flow.envWith` takes a selector, not a type or a tag: `Flow.envWith _.Clock`. `'env` is an ordinary F# record,
  so there is no type-directed service lookup and no `Flow.service`.
- Declare a per-service contract (an interface `IHasFoo` exposing one member `Foo`) only when a package must ask
  for a service without knowing the caller's record type. Read it through the package's `service` accessor.
- Run with `Flow.run`, `Flow.startTask`, or `Flow.toAsync`; `to*` starts nothing, `start*` begins immediately.
- Use `Layer` plus `Layer.provide` from `Axial.Layers` when building the environment is
  effectful. `Flow.scoped` and the `Flow.scope...` resource operations are core and work without layers.
- Use `Flow.fromTask`/`fromAsync` when thrown exceptions are defects; use `attemptTask`/`attemptAsync` when expected
  exceptions belong in the typed failure channel. These take a cancellable factory; `awaitStartedTask` wraps work
  that is already running.
- `Bind.error` and `Bind.mapError` create markers consumed by `let!`, `do!`, or `return!` in `flow { }`; use them only
  where a source error needs assignment or mapping at that bind site.
- `Policy<'env,'error,'input,'output>` is a reusable environment-aware verification function. Run it as a workflow
  step with `Flow.verify`; use `Bind` instead for one-time bind-site error adaptation.
- Execute finite roots with `App.run`. Use `App.start` when an outer host owns stopping and awaits cleanup.

## Effects and resources

- Process and HttpClient implementations perform only their named `IProcess` or `IHttp` effect. Inject clock,
  randomness, GUID, environment-variable, filesystem, console, and other operational effects explicitly.
- Use `use` and `use!` for lexical disposal. Use `Flow.scoped` to create a runtime ownership boundary, then
  `Flow.scopeAcquireRelease`, `Flow.scopeResource`, `Flow.scopeDisposable`, or a finalizer operation to attach cleanup.
  A scoped resource is anything registered this way, plus what Axial registers for you (a hub subscription, a
  `Queue.makeScoped` queue, a forked fiber); it is released when the scope it was registered with closes.
- Scoped resources in concurrent code:
  - When you receive a concurrent flow's value, you also receive its scoped resources.
  - When you don't receive the value, its scoped resources are released.
  - `zipPar`, `sequencePar`, `traversePar`, and `forEachPar` move them to the caller's scope when every flow succeeds
    and release them when any fails. `race` keeps the winner's and releases the loser's. `timeout` keeps them only
    when the flow succeeds in time.
- Use `Flow.fork`, `join`, and `interrupt` for owned fibers; `forkDetached` states intentional fire-and-forget.
  `fork` returns a handle, not a value, so the fiber releases its scoped resources when it settles: a resource
  returned through `Fiber.join` is already released. To acquire one resource in the background and keep it, use
  `Flow.forkResource resource` and `Fiber.join` it later. To acquire several in parallel, use `zipPar` or
  `sequencePar` of `Flow.scopeResource`.
- In ZIO 2 or Effect, a forked fiber shares the parent's `Scope`; in Axial it owns its own, like
  `ZIO.scoped(effect).fork`. Translate forking an `acquireRelease` and joining it later to `Flow.forkResource`;
  `Axial.Guardrails` reports the forked form as `AXG007`. `zipPar`, `race`, and parallel traversals match ZIO and
  Effect for values you receive. What losers and failed branches acquired is released at once, not when the scope
  closes, so a reference such a flow stored elsewhere (a `Ref`, a field) points at a released resource.
- Use `Flow.retry` for typed failures, `Flow.repeat` for successful repetition, `FlowStream` for effectful pull
  streams, and STM for composable transactional coordination.
- Use `Queue` to hand values between fibers when there is exactly one logical consumer. `Queue.make` takes a
  `QueueStrategy` (`BackPressure n` suspends producers when full, `Dropping n` discards the newest value, `Sliding n`
  evicts the oldest, `Unbounded`); `Queue.bounded n` and friends are shorthands. Offer with `Queue.offer`; take,
  batch (`Dequeue.takeBetween 1 500`), and shut down with the `Dequeue` functions, which accept a `Queue`.
  `Dequeue.shutdown` lets the consumer drain its backlog, and `FlowStream.fromDequeue` ends normally after shutdown
  and drain.
- Use `Hub` when there can be zero or many consumers; use `Queue` for exactly one logical consumer. Each
  `Hub.subscribe` chooses its own `QueueStrategy`, returns a `Dequeue`, and belongs to the current scope (a forked
  fiber's subscription ends with the fiber); `Dequeue.shutdown` unsubscribes. Only a full `BackPressure` subscription
  suspends `Hub.publish`, and while it waits no subscriber gets later values; `Hub.tryPublish` never waits.
- Use `Flow.forkGraceful (Dequeue.shutdown queue) grace` for a consumer that must drain its queue when its scope
  closes.
- Connect streams to queues and hubs with `FlowStream.fromDequeue`, `fromHub strategy` (subscribes for the life of the
  stream), `runIntoQueue`, and `runIntoHub`. `FlowStream.mergePar` runs streams concurrently, `buffer strategy`
  decouples a producer from its consumer, and `fromSchedule` turns a schedule into a tick stream.
- Attach cleanup to one flow with `Flow.ensuring` (always), `Flow.onExit` (sees the `Exit`), or `Flow.onInterrupt`;
  handlers run without the flow's cancellation. `Flow.never` waits until interrupted.
- Use `SubscriptionRef` (namespace `Axial.State`) for current state that consumers join late:
  `SubscriptionRef.changes strategy` streams the current value and then every update, with no gap or duplicate.
- Cap backoff with `Schedule.exponential d |> Schedule.union (Schedule.spaced cap)`; bound attempts with
  `Schedule.recurs n |> Schedule.intersect (Schedule.exponential d)`. Use `Schedule.fixedRate period` for drift-free
  periodic work; `Schedule.spaced` waits after each run instead.
- The torture tests (`/concurrency-and-state/torture-tests/index.html`, runnable from `examples/Axial.TortureTest`)
  are worked examples of every concurrency construct under interruption, failure, and shutdown. Each page lists the
  invariants the construct guarantees.

## Processes

- Open `Axial.Process.DSL` for `cmd`, `cwd`, `env`, routing/capture helpers, and `=>`. Interpolation holes are
  individual native arguments; `bash`, `sh`, and `pwsh` explicitly opt into shell syntax with values passed separately.
- Configure a `ProcessCommand` before connecting it. `=>` connects native streams; `pipeTo` is its pipeline form.
  Use `mapFinalCommand` for the final command of a connected spec, and `stageDefaults` for overridable fallbacks.
- Routing and capture are independent. `toFlow` captures full stdout and separate 64 KiB stderr tails; stream
  constructors default to 64 KiB tails. `captureAll`/`captureTail`/`captureNothing` affect stdout only; stderr has
  explicit `captureStderr*` helpers. Stderr joins stdout only through `mergeStderr` or a combined-channel pipe.
- `streamStdoutLines` produces a completion-aware `ProcessStream`. Keep `ProcessStream` transformations and
  terminals to retain `Completed result` or awaited `StoppedEarly`; `toFlowStream` deliberately drops completion.
  Effectful consumers use `runForEachFlow` or `runFoldFlow`, with process and consumer errors kept distinct.
- `Process.tryRun`/`Process.tryRunWith` return `Exit` for commands, specs, or Flows; `Process.run`/`Process.runWith`
  return the successful value and raise `ProcessRunException` on failure. These boundary helpers are not DSL aliases.
  Direct commands retain batch output; existing Flows keep their policies. `toFlow` needs `IHasProcess`;
  streaming additionally needs `IHasClock`.
- `mergeStdout` fans in producer lines; `captureParallel` captures independent commands with bounded workflow
  concurrency and ordered results. Use `flow { }` for sequencing and `Flow.orElseWith` for typed recovery.
- Guides: `/process/index.html`, `/process/scripts.html`, `/process/streaming.html`, and `/process/dsl-recipes.html`.

## Hosts

- `Axial.Hosting` is .NET-only.
- `Axial.Hosting.Node` is Fable JavaScript for Node only.
- `Axial.Hosting.Browser` is Fable JavaScript for browsers only.
- Core Flow is supported in Fable JavaScript on both Node and browsers.

See `/notes/packages-and-platforms.html` for the complete package matrix and `/notes/package-maturity.html` for ratings and application evidence.
